name: geant4_depth_dose_simulation
description: Monte Carlo depth-dose simulation with GEANT4: fire a particle beam into a slab of one NIST material and get the energy deposited in each depth bin, plus the peak depth (the Bragg peak for ions). Use it for range and shielding questions — how deep a 150 MeV proton beam deposits its dose in water, how much of a gamma beam a lead slab absorbs, how an ion's range changes with energy or tissue. One fixed application is compiled against the local GEANT4 on first use; nothing but the numbers below can vary, so no geometry or macro is accepted. Requires a local GEANT4 installation with its physics data (geant4-config on PATH, or GEANT4_CONFIG set); a 200-event proton run takes about a second.

energy_mev.description: Kinetic energy of each primary particle in MeV, from 0.001 to 100000 (default 150).

material.description: Target material, a NIST name GEANT4 builds itself (default 'G4_WATER').

thickness_cm.description: Depth of the target along the beam in cm, from 0.01 to 500 (default 20). Make it larger than the expected range, or the beam leaves the target before stopping.

bins.description: Number of equal depth bins to score, from 1 to 2000 (default 100). thickness_cm / bins is the depth resolution.

events.description: Primary particles to simulate, from 1 to 200000 (default 200). More events mean a smoother curve and a longer run.

timeout_seconds.description: Give up after this many seconds, from 1 to 1800 (default 600).
